item.title: Autonomous stabilization of many-body entanglement with Floquet Hamiltonians and weak measurement
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Interleaving Floquet engineering with weak measurement autonomously stabilizes nuclear spin squeezing down to −12.8 dB below the standard quantum limit (R=0.9) and collective Schrödinger-cat states with fidelity >0.9.

Grade 0.473 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Charlotte Franke, Dorian A. Gangloff

Figure

Squeezing parameter ξR2 and cat infidelity 1−ℱ versus evolution time and stroboscopic cycle number M, showing autonomous relaxation to steady-state floors below the standard quantum limit.

Asks

How can Floquet Hamiltonian engineering be combined with engineered dissipation without continuous reservoir noise disrupting the coherent drive?

But

Simulated in central-spin systems with weak non-collinear coupling Anc/ωn≪1, per-cycle measurement strength ϵ≤0.1, and nuclear ensemble dephasing T2≈1 ms to 100 ms.

Tools

Floquet Hamiltonian engineering · stroboscopic weak measurement · central-spin quantum dot model · Lindblad master equation · adiabatic elimination

Abstract

Reaching a technological advantage with large quantum systems requires safeguarding their many-body entanglement. Dissipation typically acts to decohere a quantum system via random projective noise but, when judiciously engineered together with coherent interactions, it can funnel the system towards a target entangled state. The native interactions and dissipative channels available to most systems are, however, difficult to combine effectively. Here we propose interleaving Floquet Hamiltonian engineering, which allows the construction of non-native coherent interactions, with weak measurement, which enables a tuneable dissipative channel, to enable programmable and autonomous stabilization of many-body entanglement. We show this analytically and numerically for the central-spin system of a semiconductor quantum dot, for which we construct spin-squeezed and Schrödinger-cat states that are stabilized against realistic levels of dephasing. Our approach is applicable to any system compatible with periodic drives and tuneable measurement strength and could enable novel approaches to practical error correction.

item.title: Experimental Measurement and Theoretical Analysis of Energy Relaxation Rates of an Interacting Two-Qubit System on a D-Wave Quantum Annealer
item.description:
Long shot new result — Energy relaxation rates of first excited states in interacting two-qubit systems on a D-Wave annealer are predicted within a factor of ≈4 using local relaxation parameters calibrated from uncoupled single-qubit reference measurements.

Grade 0.417 · 1.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Yusei Amano, Sorato Suzuki, Hiroki Kuji, Tetsuro Nikuni, Takashi Imoto, Yuichiro Matsuzaki

Figure

Predicted versus experimentally measured energy relaxation rates for interacting two-qubit systems, showing predictions calibrated from uncoupled single-qubit data track measurements within a factor of approximately four.

Asks

Can relaxation measurements of constituent physical qubits performed with interaction turned off predict the energy relaxation rate of the interacting multiqubit system?

But

Low-temperature limit retaining only downward transitions; transitions near 1.5 GHz; neglects inter-qubit noise correlations; model systematically underestimates relaxation rates in the small-transition-matrix-element regime.

Tools

D-Wave Advantage 4.1 quantum annealer · Reverse-annealing protocol · GKSL master equation with independent local σ^z-noise · Exact diagonalization

Abstract

In D-Wave quantum annealers, various properties of the ground state have been clarified, whereas the correspondence between theory and experiment for energy relaxation rates in multiqubit excited states remains insufficiently understood. Here, we measured the energy relaxation rates of the first excited states in single-qubit systems and interacting two-qubit systems using a D-Wave quantum annealer. We analyzed the measured relaxation rates using a Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad master equation with independent local σ^z-type noise channels. The calculated relaxation rates reproduced the overall trends observed experimentally, supporting the model at a qualitative level. We then used the relaxation rates measured for the uncoupled single-qubit systems to calibrate the local relaxation parameters and predict the relaxation rates of the interacting two-qubit systems. The predicted rates remained within a factor of approximately four of the measured rates. These results show that the relaxation measurements on individual qubits can provide a practical estimate of relaxation in small interacting quantum systems and may help clarify relaxation mechanisms in programmable quantum annealers.

item.title: Transport statistics and thermoelectric performance of Hofstadters butterfly
item.description:
Long shot theory — Optimal lead-system coupling τL=τR=4τ in a finite Hofstadter lattice yields near-unit transmission plateaus T(ω)≈1 via topologically protected boundary modes, violating standard thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounds and enhancing thermoelectric power and cooling currents.

Grade 0.406 · 1.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “transmon and fluxonium coherence, single- and two-qubit gate fidelity” · Friedemann Queißer, Gernot Schaller

Figure

Dimensionless output power P and cooling current IQ (top), along with efficiency η and coefficient of performance κ (bottom), plotted against dimensionless bias voltage across a finite Hofstadter system.

Asks

How do non-equilibrium transport statistics and thermoelectric performance behave across finite-size Hofstadter lattices coupled to reservoirs?

But

Non-interacting single-particle transport, single-site lead-to-system contacts, stationary regime.

Tools

Non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) · Levitov-Lesovik counting statistics · Hofstadter lattice Hamiltonian · Tight-binding semi-infinite chain leads

Abstract

We investigate electrons subject to a magnetic field that may tunnel along a square lattice and additionally to two electronic leads. Using non-equilibrium Greens functions we evaluate the transmission and from that particle and energy currents and zero-frequency noise of the setup. We identify sweet spots for which the transmission reaches unity over broad frequency windows -- carried by topologically protected boundary modes that are quite robust against local fluctuations of on-site energies. These transmission plateaus can be exploited for the implementation robust current standards, clocks and thermoelectric devices.
